methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia's AI challenge isn't data centers. It's small-business adoption | Guest column - Richmond Times-Dispatch
signals.signal_reading: Guest column explicitly identifies small-business AI adoption as Virginia's real challenge, signaling that infrastructure investment (data centers) is concentrating in metro areas while practical AI capability remains shallow and inaccessible to the broader economy.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on Richmond's young workforce indicates deepening capability demands in metro hubs, likely attracting talent from rural areas and reinforcing concentration of AI-adjacent skills in urban centers.

signals.title: University of Virginia Students Help Businesses Explore AI - GovTech
signals.signal_reading: UVA students helping businesses explore AI represents peer-to-peer knowledge transfer and capacity building beyond infrastructure—a potential distribution mechanism if it reaches beyond Charlottesville to smaller communities and businesses statewide.

signals.title: Norfolk looks to add AI dispatcher tool for non-emergency calls - WAVY.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk deploying turnkey AI dispatcher tools for non-emergency calls demonstrates platform-delivered AI adoption in municipal services—shallow implementation but distributed benefit, potentially replicable across Virginia localities without deep technical expertise.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - 12onyourside.com
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ investment adding 200 jobs in Henrico for AI data center infrastructure deepens Richmond's technical ecosystem, but concentrates high-skill employment in metro areas while distributing only indirect economic benefits and energy grid strain.
